The 2 loss of one tank will only reduce the hub’s storage capacity by 9%. That will reduce the storage margin versus the CO ship slightly but not enough to affect the hub’s or the ships’ throughput. Choosing to design 2 T-RICH with fewer, larger tanks, such as four spheres, would result in a significant 25% loss of storage capacity if one tank goes offline. To minimize hub downtime due to unplanned failure of critical parts, the plant’s sparing philosophy would be aggressive in making sure that ample critical spare parts are always on hand, and the plant’s operating staff is well-trained to replace parts themselves as quickly as possible. Aptamus’ affiliate company OSG is well versed in keeping critical spare parts on hand for its fleet of petroleum tankers where each day out of service can result in over $100,000 in lost revenue and harm the company’s reputation. The T-RICH hub would follow OSG’s aggressive sparing philosophy in order to minimize downtime. Spares will be categorized into the following types: Page86 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version  Capital Spares  Construction Spares  Startup and Commissioning Spares  Operating Spares 4.9 ALTERNATIVES AND SENSITIVITIES CONSIDERED Due to a fairly well-defined range of options presented during the initial project kick-off, the number of alternatives considered during this phase was minimal. Plant capacity was defined and well aligned with the liquid CO carrier ship size, and identification by Aptamus that they had identified Medium Pressure 2 as the selected CO transport condition meant that storage conditions were not subject to optimization. 2 As the selected site was more than suitable for the plant requirements, there was no requirement to look at alternate locations. Liquefaction technology has historically been subject to selection. However, previous experience has indicated that Internal Refrigeration as a proven dispatchable technology generally forms a robust base case design. Power and Cooling duties of Internal and External refrigeration plants typically have similar requirements and equipment counts. Ultimately, for the purposes of this study, it was agreed that the base case of internal refrigeration would be retained for the duration of the work, and if necessary revisited at later stages. Specific areas where additional focus was required were:  Storage Configuration (number, size, and orientation of liquid CO storage vessels) 2  Cooling Demand and Power Consumption (Designing for the worst case ambient temperature exaggerates annual power demand, and work is required to provide a more realistic figure)  Construction Approach (site specific constraints meant a number of options were examined) 4.9.1 STORAGE ALTERNATIVES Selecting the number of, type, and configuration of liquid CO storage tanks was addressed by 2 development of a base case and performing a capital cost comparison vs the base case.
